heading: EXT. BAKER'S YARD - PUDDING LANE, LONDON - NIGHT - 1666

units.text: EXT. BAKER'S YARD - PUDDING LANE, LONDON - NIGHT - 1666
A narrow courtyard hemmed by timber houses leaning toward each other like drunken gossips.
The oven door glows red.
Upwind, over the rooftops, the sky has begun to bloom a dull and sullen orange.
THOMAS FARRINER (50s, baker, flour to the elbow) stands at the oven mouth with a wooden peel, sliding out the last loaf of the night.
His wife ALICE FARRINER (40s, shawl over a nightdress) bangs the shutters closed one by one.
Their daughter MARGERY (12, barefoot, hair undone) clutches a cat to her chest by the well.
The apprentice JEREMIAH PICKLE (16, soot-faced) hauls buckets across the cobbles, slopping water.
Beside the gate, a neighbor, WIDOW CATHERINE MOLINEUX (60s, nightcap, rosary), stands with her mouth moving in silent prayer.
And out of the shadows, a stranger on a gray horse, the King's messenger, SIR HUGH WAINWRIGHT (40s, mud to the thighs, a sealed letter in his gauntlet), reins in at the gate.
Master Farriner! By the King's order, put out your oven.
units.name: WAINWRIGHT

units.text: It's out, sir. Near enough.
units.name: THOMAS

units.text: Near enough has burned a parish.
units.name: WAINWRIGHT

units.text: Thomas turns to Jeremiah, who has frozen with a bucket in each hand.
Alice drops the last shutter-bar.
Margery tightens her grip on the cat, which squirms and yowls.
Thomas.
units.name: ALICE

units.text: I hear.
units.name: THOMAS

units.text: Look at the sky.
units.name: ALICE

units.text: He does not look.
He keeps his eyes on the horseman.
The widow's rosary clicks.
The orange in the sky deepens; a distant bell begins to toll, then another, then three at once.
The fire is at Fish Street. It will be at the Bridge by dawn.
units.name: WAINWRIGHT

units.text: Papa, are we to leave?
units.name: MARGERY

units.text: We are not.
units.name: THOMAS

units.text: Thomas.
units.name: ALICE

units.text: We are not leaving my oven.
units.name: THOMAS

units.text: Master Farriner, I have orders.
units.name: WAINWRIGHT

units.text: Then read them.
units.name: THOMAS

units.text: Wainwright breaks the seal and reads silently.
Thomas wipes his hands on his apron, and Alice, seeing it, steps forward and takes the loaf from the peel and presses it into Margery's arms beside the cat.
Jeremiah sets down the buckets and begins, without being told, to untie the oven's iron door.
The order is plain. Quit the lane. All of you.
units.name: WAINWRIGHT

units.text: Where do we go, sir?
units.name: THOMAS

units.text: North. Moorfields.
units.name: WAINWRIGHT

units.text: Silence.
The bells swell.
A glowing ember lands on the stones at Catherine's feet.
She crosses herself and steps on it.
God keep this house.
units.name: CATHERINE

units.text: He will, Catherine. Come with us.
units.name: ALICE

units.text: I'll bring my chair.
units.name: CATHERINE

units.text: Thomas takes one last look at the oven.
Its mouth glows like an eye closing.
He lays the peel across the sill, and lifts the latch of the gate.
Jeremiah. Take the handcart.
units.name: THOMAS

units.text: Yes, Master.
units.name: JEREMIAH

units.text: Thomas offers Alice his arm.
She takes it.
They file out into the lane, the cat wailing, the loaf warm in Margery's arms, and the orange glow licking down the rooftops behind them.
